title: secp256k1-ecdlp: inversion-batched parallel double-or-add walk at birthday exponent 1

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the inversion-batched parallel double-or-add walk in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^128.988644 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^120.084963 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^20.001442 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. Each walk step is charged as one reference batched incomplete affine addition at the fixed price C=1000, plus the residual field multiplication, inversion slack, coefficient update and distinguished-point insert bound in proof.md. The random-mapping calculation gives a collision probability above 0.632 at this budget; the claimed probability is the 0.39 floor. Inputs that miss the collision run the full step budget. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps or endomorphism speedup. This is an analytic generic accounting control, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check the double-or-add coefficient update on a small additive cyclic group: every invertible collision recovers the secret, and the step budget meets steps*(steps-1) >= 2*order. On order 1009 the observed recovery rate inside that budget is at least 0.39. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
